syllabus.clause: Kahn's in-degree queue vs reverse DFS finish order

at.step: Kahn's algorithm repeatedly removes a vertex with in-degree zero and decrements its neighbours' in-degrees, using a plain queue — the same queue mechanics already built for breadth-first search, pointed at in-degrees instead of distances.

Reverse DFS finish order runs the same depth-first search already built, then reads off vertices in decreasing finish time. It gives a second, independently valid topological order — not required to match Kahn's vertex-for-vertex, only to respect every edge.

Kahn's algorithm cannot be run to completion — vertices remain stuck with positive in-degree, none ever reaching zero — exactly when the graph has a cycle. Reverse DFS already has its own back-edge test built in. Neither algorithm needs a separate cycle check bolted on.
